chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim and al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abi Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the Qaim (peace be upon him) arises, he will come with a system/unprecedented matter unlike that which was before.

key_terms.الْقَـٰئِمُ: The Qaim (The Riser), a title for the Mahdi

ai.seo_question: What is unique about the governance or system of the Qaim al-Mahdi upon his rise?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) highlighting the transformative nature of the Mahdi’s rise, where he establishes a novel order ('amr') distinct from prior historical epochs. This 'newness' signifies not merely a change in leadership but a fundamental restructuring of societal and spiritual governance, fulfilling the eschatological promise of universal justice. The emphasis on 'non-what-was' underscores the unique, divinely ordained character of his rule, setting it apart from previous prophetic or caliphal systems.
